![Hebrew Alphabet Wall Poster With Letters' Pronunciation ...](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/10140757-2762-0139-0000-d23a9583224e:4)
The Hebrew alphabet (the *Alef-Bet* ) has **22 consonant letters** , reads from **right to left** , and traditionally uses vowel marks called **nikkud** (dots and dashes) to guide pronunciation , though modern Hebrew is mostly written without them.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_alphabet)[[2]](https://mena-languages.northwestern.edu/language-learning/languages-with-different-scripts/hebrew-alphabet.html)

You can explore full interactive pronunciation charts at [AlephBet](https://learnhebrewalphabet.com/sounds/) or check out guides via [Dictionary.co.il](https://dictionary.co.il/pronunciation_guide.php).[[1]](https://learnhebrewalphabet.com/sounds/)[[2]](https://dictionary.co.il/pronunciation_guide.php)



---

### Core Letter Pronunciations (Modern Israeli Standard)
| Letter | Name | Pronunciation / Sound Guide |
|---|---|---|
| **א** | Alef | Silent (takes the sound of its vowel) |
| **ב** | Bet / Vet | "b" as in boy (with dot) / "v" as in vine (without dot) |
| **ג** | Gimel | "g" as in go |
| **ד** | Dalet | "d" as in dog |
| **ה** | Hey | "h" as in hat |
| **ו** | Vav | "v" as in vine, or acts as "o"/"u" vowel |
| **ז** | Zayin | "z" as in zebra |
| **ח** | Chet | Guttural "ch" (throat clearing sound like German *Bach*) |
| **ט** | Tet | "t" as in top |
| **י** | Yod | "y" as in yes |
| **כ / ך** | Kaf / Final Kaf | "k" as in king / "kh" guttural at the end of a word |
| **ל** | Lamed | "l" as in lamp |
| **מ / ם** | Mem / Final Mem | "m" as in moon |
| **נ / ן** | Nun / Final Nun | "n" as in nice |
| **ס** | Samech | "s" as in sun |
| **ע** | Ayin | Often silent or a glottal stop |
| **פ / ף** | Pe / Final Pe | "p" as in pen / "f" as in fish |
| **צ / ץ** | Tsadi / Final Tsadi | "ts" as in cats |
| **ק** | Qof | "k" as in king |
| **ר** | Resh | Hebrew "r" (often made in the back of the throat/mouth) |
| **ש** | Shin / Sin | "sh" as in ship / "s" as in sun |
| **ת** | Tav | "t" as in top |



---

### Key Rules to Keep in Mind

- **Final Letters (Sofit):** Five letters (*Kaf, Mem, Nun, Pe, Tsadi* ) change their shape when they appear at the very end of a word, though their base sound stays the same.
- **The Dagesh:** A dot inside certain letters (like Bet, Kaf, and Pe) hardens or alters their sound (e.g., *v* becomes *b*).
- **Vowels:** Written Hebrew primarily relies on consonants; vowel points (*nikkud* ) are mostly used in poetry, children's books, prayers, and beginner texts.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ekc3lIVdHEU)[[2]](https://mena-languages.northwestern.edu/language-learning/languages-with-different-scripts/hebrew-alphabet.html)[[3]](https://www.chabad.org/library/article_cdo/aid/4069287/jewish/The-Hebrew-Alphabet.htm)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZnZ3tj4l43Y&t=520)
